analysis.title: GS Basics - Tech Rotation. FCF Inflection. Labor/AI
key_insights: Samsung's results disappointed, mainly because it announced no shareholder returns against a higher bar set after Hynix. Advantest rose sharply on a significant guidance upgrade, which the desk reads as a reminder of robust AI demand.

Hyperscaler earnings were messy on headlines but the compute trajectory is intact. One mega cap platform fell about 10% after hours on consumer ad misses while its Cloud growth stayed robust. The second beat whisper numbers on core cloud, produced positive quarterly FCF and grew total contracted obligations.

The second platform's light capex reflected the timing of third-party facility deliveries, not weaker appetite, and next quarter is guided higher. Aggregate spending intentions across both platforms are flat to higher, with power and cluster delivery as the main bottlenecks.

The market has stopped questioning whether capex is durable. The open question is value capture: whether cheaper model running costs lift hyperscaler returns on capital or expand gross margins for enterprise applications.

Oracle is called the most important development for credit. The stock rallied double digits after management laid out positive FCF in H2 FY28 and $30bn+ in FY29, with capex stepping down in FY29. Incremental capital raises are capped at $20bn through FY30, excluding refinancing.

Oracle guided to non-GAAP operating margins of 40%+ by FY30 on $225bn+ of revenue, with high-20s project returns and about $16bn of annualized revenue per fully ramped gigawatt. The desk says this depends on execution, utilization and financing assumptions, and that credit spreads have not yet responded.

The Fed meeting under Warsh was read as balanced. He referred directly to tightening financial conditions early in the press conference. Cook and Hammack dissented hawkishly, but Logan staying put was a positive surprise. The growth assessment was upgraded and inflation is still elevated. December still looks like a hike, with little reason for material repricing. The desk calls it a volatility-suppressing event.

The ECB has hiked twice since June and the question is whether December brings a third. French sovereign stress is tightening conditions for them. With European gas touching €100/MWh, the desk does not expect a dovish pivot, though there is room for repricing if financial conditions get more attention.

On energy and geopolitics, Vance's letter to Iran looks like a last-minute attempt at a diplomatic win, but Iran's position is resolute. The desk thinks the path leads to escalation after the midterms. European equities are looking through €100 gas and elevated oil, which suggests the market expects the squeeze not to last.

Positioning: the pain trade is hyperscalers underperforming while de-risked picks and shovels start working. Advantest's upgrade and supportive overnight optical developments reinforce the micro picture. The desk expects dips to be bought.

Credit is the most important thing to watch. Stability is improving, and Oracle may matter more for the levered infrastructure complex than either hyperscaler print. The market is moving from rewarding capex growth to demanding evidence of returns.
A pre-midterm US/Iran meeting is described as the geopolitical lottery ticket, an enormous positive surprise if it happens.
